messages.subject: ggplot2 faceting of pictures
parts:
I am recently new to using R within this year. I bought the book on
ggplot2 and have been loving the package a lot.
I have two questions regarding ggplot2.

The first is about graphing pictures. I used hadley's code in the book
for fortifying images that were loaded with the EBimage package.
I got ggplot2 to plot a nice picture of some microscopy images. What I
would like to do it to bind each image to a particular row of a
dataframe of conditions and then facet plot 4 to 8 images on one graph
in ggplot2. I have not been able to figure out a way to do this
without coercing each image into a dataframe and then rind them all
into one dataframe. This however is too much memory consumed and gives
many errors.
Is there is a way with the fortify method of plotting multiple
pictures faceted in ggplot2?

My second question is about facet_grid.
I have been using it to plot several factors of conditions on my data.
Such as the following:
facet_grid(Wash ~ Cell_Line + Butyrate)
the facet labels are not what I would expect
I get a set of facet labels that make no sense the column headers
should be 1st condition above the second condition Cell_Line over
Butyrate, but that is not what I get

Am I doing something wrong or does ggplot2 have a bug in it that
doesn’t work when facet_grid uses multiple items for either the row or
column facets?


Many Thanks

This is a known bug, I believe. The plot should be correct, but the
labels will not be. See:
http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/labels/bug#issue/87

Here is one option as a way to circumvent the issue:

# Example using mtcars data
dat <- with(mtcars, data.frame(mpg, hp, cyl = factor(cyl),
vs = factor(vs), am = factor(am),
vsam = factor(paste(am, vs, sep = "\n"))))


library(ggplot2)
# using vs + am works, but incorrect labels
ggplot(data = dat, aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) + geom_point() +
facet_grid(cyl ~ vs + am)
# using vsam, works with correct labels
ggplot(data = dat, aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) + geom_point() +
facet_grid(cyl ~ vsam)

Cheers,

Josh
